findings.title: An invalid retiresAt on the ACTIVE seat still has no defined behavior after R4
findings.detail: Lines 8/25/29 define invalid retiresAt only as 「不可选」 — a candidate-side notion (verifyAndRankCandidates skips name === snapshot.activeName at account-candidate-selector.ts:179; selectNextAccount filters account.name === input.currentName at account-store.ts:498/532). R2 line 25 made the ACTIVE account's retiresAt load-bearing for a forced account_dead switch + terminal quarantine, and R4 (lines 58-63) revised only the throttle, so this is still open. Fail-open and fail-closed are opposite behaviors and both are defensible from the pinned text. The most likely operator slip is exactly the one the new strict validator rejects: `-0700` instead of `-07:00`, or a date-only `2026-09-14` — and line 32/48 keep the production write a hand edit with the lock-respecting setter deferred. Recommend one sentence: an unparseable/offset-less retiresAt on the active account is NOT treated as retired (fail-open, since `retiresAt <= now` cannot be satisfied by a non-instant), plus an operator-visible marker on the capacity/patrol row so the misconfiguration is not silent. Also pin that the shared helper takes `unknown` and rejects non-strings — readStoreStrict (account-store.ts:686-719) type-checks name/quotaExhaustedUntil/weeklyResetAt/switchCooldownUntil/unavailable but would pass `retiresAt: 1789000000000` or `retiresAt: {}` through untouched.

findings.title: R4 pins where the early snapshot goes but not whether it replaces the existing read at quota-monitor.ts:1672
findings.detail: Line 61 says 「early snapshot 放在 local_scan 提前返回之前」. Today the only locked snapshot is `const snapshot = await deps.withAccountsLock(() => deps.readSnapshot())` at quota-monitor.ts:1672, i.e. AFTER the local_scan return at 1643-1657 and after `state.nextUsageDueAt = now + pollIntervalMs(...)` at 1659. The plan never says whether the hoisted read replaces 1672 or is an additional read. If it is additional, every usage-due pass takes the accounts lock twice and calls readKeychain() twice (quota-monitor-runtime.ts:538-551), and the two snapshots can disagree: handleAccountDead would be handed the early snapshot's `store.generation` while commitSuccessfulObservation/candidateDecisionInputs downstream use the later one — and switch-executor.ts:886-893 fails an account_dead switch with reasonCode `active_marker_drift` on exactly that mismatch. Separately, even in the replace-it form the plan should state the new cadence explicitly: readSnapshot (readStore + resolveMachineAccount + readKeychain) under withAccountsLock moves from ~every basePollMinutes=20 to every paneScanSeconds=60 (quota-monitor-config.ts), a ~20x increase in lock acquisitions and Keychain reads, against a lock that switch-executor holds across fenced Keychain writes with a 1s heartbeat. Pin 'single snapshot per pass, reused by both the retirement check and the usage path', and add the R3-requested tests for (a) unresolved authority + usage not due still returns local_scan, (b) activeCredential null/expired still reaches the retirement check, (c) backoffUntilMs > now still reaches it.

findings.title: 「warning 不路由 founder」 is only true if the alert kind is named; a NEW kind pings the founder after a rollback
findings.detail: Line 62 pins the constraint but not the mechanism, and the two obvious implementations differ. Verified: ROUTING in quota-monitor-alert.ts:57-93 is `satisfies Record<QuotaMonitorAlertKind, RoutingPolicy>`, so adding a kind is compile-forced to carry a routing entry on the NEW binary — but the durable outbox is not kind-gated: parseAlertOutbox (quota-monitor-state.ts:885-886) accepts any kind matching /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/, so a queued-but-undelivered retirement warning survives a binary rollback intact, and the OLD binary's lookup `(ROUTING as Record<string, RoutingPolicy>)[alert.kind] ?? { mention: true, severe: true }` (quota-monitor-alert.ts:218-224) resolves a mention target from FLYWHEEL_QUOTA_ALERT_MENTION_USER / FLYWHEEL_FOUNDER_USER_ID and duplicates into the severe channel — i.e. it mentions the founder, which is precisely what line 62 forbids. Reusing an existing mention:false/severe:false kind (e.g. quota_monitor_down) makes the constraint structural instead of emergent. Note the kind is also part of lead-alert.sh's eventId sha1(project|lead|kind|signature), so it is part of the dedup key the same line depends on. Name the kind in the plan and pin a test asserting mention=false.

findings.title: The plan pins two contradictory host-verification contracts; the handoff cannot honestly cite both
findings.detail: Line 13 commits to `pnpm lint`, `pnpm -r build` and `pnpm test:packages:run` on the host (all three exist in root package.json). Line 43 says host scope is targeted tests + lint/build with the full suite left to exact-head CI. R3 raised this as LOW and R4 (line 65: 「此修订只解决新暴露的 HIGH」) did not reconcile it, so both sentences are still pinned. This matters beyond tidiness: the handoff statement of 'what was actually run' will be read as the superset, and a locally-green focused suite is not a CI-green head. Delete or supersede line 13's suite list so the narrower claim is the only one written down, and state that the QA PASS gate is the CI conclusion on the exact pushed head.

findings.title: min-deadline selection over a path that bypasses the anti-flap gate still has no floor on switch frequency
findings.detail: Line 25 selects the 「min-deadline 候选」 and line 9 ranks by min(resetMs, retiresAtMs), so the selector deliberately prefers the candidate closest to its own retirement. Confirmed the retirement switch runs through handleAccountDead (quota-monitor.ts:1355-1500), which is reached at 1748 and never passes the `now - state.lastSwitchAt < minSwitchIntervalMinutes * 60_000` gate at 1884-1890 — that gate sits only on the quota/model path after the usage read. If two subscriptions share a billing date (business 00:00, personal 00:05), the fleet switches onto personal and then off it minutes later: two Keychain writes, two runner-pane disruptions, two terminal `unavailable` quarantines and two founder notifications, with nothing in the design bounding N. R3 raised this and R4 scoped it out. Today only one account is slated to carry retiresAt so the probability is low, but the cheap fix is one sentence — either a minimum remaining-life threshold before a retiring candidate is ranked first, or an explicit acceptance of the storm with a test pinning the observed behavior.

findings.title: The revive-window clamp names one epoch site; there are two — but the practical blast radius is smaller than R3 stated
findings.detail: Line 41 speaks of 「既有 revive 窗口」 in the singular. state.reviveEpoch is created at two sites: quota-monitor.ts:2179-2186 (account trigger) and quota-incident.ts finalizeModelSwitch (model-cap trigger). Naming both costs one clause. Correcting the severity with evidence, though: reviveScan's authorization is `epoch !== null && epoch.generation === state.observedGeneration && !input.monitorOnly` (quota-revive-scan.ts:311-321), and any switch bumps observedGeneration, so a stale epoch whose source later retires is already dead by generation; and `sourceAccount` itself appears only in an alert body string (quota-revive-scan.ts:384), not in any gating decision. So an unclamped model epoch degrades to a misleading alert line rather than an unauthorized revive. Worth a sentence in the plan, not worth a round.

findings.title: Follow-up is correctly parked, but there is a second founder-facing surface and one correction to the R3 record
findings.detail: Line 47 parks earliestReset. Confirmed earliestReset (account-store.ts:865-894) filters neither auth nor retirement, and the no-candidate retirement path routes to `no_account` with earliestReset (switch-executor.ts:1038) which account-switch-repair.ts renders as 「所有 Claude 账号都已用尽，最早 reset: ...」. A second surface the follow-up does not name: quota-guard-cli.ts:730-750 builds its 「Suggestion: flywheel-claude-profile use <name>」 from `!isAuthUnusable(entry) && isQuotaUsable(entry, nowMs)` with no retirement filter, so in the window before the quarantine mark lands — or permanently if the retirement switch never fires because machine-account authority is unresolved or the deployment is monitorOnly — it can tell an operator to switch onto a retired account. One correction to the R3 record worth carrying into the handoff: the claim that no command clears `unavailable` is wrong — `flywheel-quota-guard unavailable-clear <name> --reason ...` exists (quota-guard-cli.ts:258-305, dispatched at 775), takes the accounts lock and writes an audit record, so a wrongly-quarantined account IS recoverable without hand-editing the store. That materially lowers the risk of the quarantine-on-misconfiguration scenario; state it in the handoff rather than re-deriving it under pressure.
